articulation.def: A joint: any place where a bone meets another bone, a cartilage or a tooth. Some joints move freely and some do not move at all.

joint-structural-classes.def: The three kinds of joint sorted by what joins the bones: fibrous joints (dense connective tissue, no space), cartilaginous joints (cartilage, no space) and synovial joints (bone ends separated by a fluid-filled space lined by synovial membrane).

joint-subtypes.def: The subtypes of fibrous joint (suture between skull bones; syndesmosis, where a ligament or interosseous membrane joins two bones; gomphosis, a tooth held in its socket by the periodontal ligament) and of cartilaginous joint (synchondrosis, joined by hyaline cartilage; symphysis, joined by fibrocartilage). A joint that has turned to bone is a synostosis.

joint-functional-classes.def: The three kinds of joint sorted by how much they move: a synarthrosis is immobile or nearly so, an amphiarthrosis is slightly movable, and a diarthrosis is freely movable.
